items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Speaking of King Oliver leads me up to the impact that King Oliver had on Bubba Miley and myself... That's where Bubber got his inspiration for playing

ctx.x: Upper and lower, and I don't how he played because when he'd get tired he'd take out both plates and rest his gums. But you can see he had been quite a figure to reckon with in playing trumpet. I heard a lot of the things -- either he played them first or Louis played them first -- I don't know. He got them from Louis or Louis got them from him, and I heard some of the old things King Oliver played. Bunk, I think, was probably older than -- he may have been the same age as King Oliver. Speaking of King Oliver…

items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Joe Oliver, or Dewey Jackson, but he may be a creator

ctx.x: Yeah. And he said, 'My God, look at all this stuff.' He picked it up and tasted it, and I never saw Bunk after that because he went back to New Orleans shortly after that. But Bunk, to my mind, he wasn't one of the -- wasn't the trumpet player that Louis was or Freddy Keppard, or Joe Oliver, or Dewey Jackson, but he may be a creator -- they played so much more than he played. I'll tell you what I'll do, I have an album here, one of the albums I made with him, I think we should play his interpretation of a tune…
Okay. We'll pause here and play a track from that particular album.
